title: Conversions
content:
# Conversions

Import offline and enhanced conversions into Google Ads through the Data Manager API with POST /v1/events, and choose which conversions Google bids on with account, campaign and custom conversion goals.

import { Tab, Tabs } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/tabs';

By the end of this page, an offline conversion (deal closed, lead qualified, subscription renewed) is imported into Google Ads.

## Before you start

You need a connected `googleads` [account](/platforms/google-ads#connect) and a conversion action id. [Find a conversion action](#find-a-conversion-action) lists the ones you have.

## Send a conversion event

Call `POST /v1/events` with your `profileId`, the events, and in `destinations` the Google Ads account with the conversion action's resource name as `destinationId`.

It goes through the Data Manager API `ingestEvents` method. As of December 2025 Google recommends it for all new integrations, replacing the legacy `uploadClickConversions`.

The same endpoint handles both attribution paths:

- **Click attribution**, when you include a `gclid`, `gbraid` or `wbraid` from the originating ad click.
- **Enhanced Conversions for Leads**, when you include a hashed email or phone because no click id is available.

PII is SHA-256 hashed server-side.

For `@gmail.com` and `@googlemail.com` addresses, Zernio strips dots and `+suffix` from the local part before hashing, per Google's spec. So `john.doe+promo@gmail.com` matches `johndoe@gmail.com`.

Zernio uses the Google Ads account you already connected. There is no additional OAuth and no developer token to apply for.

<Callout type="warn">
`eventTime` is unix seconds in UTC, not milliseconds: `1798848000` is 2027-01-02T00:00:00Z. A millisecond value lands the conversion thousands of years in the future, where Google drops it.
</Callout>

`adjustmentTime` on the adjustments call below uses the same unit.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
import Zernio from '@zernio/node';

const zernio = new Zernio();

const { data: sent } = await zernio.conversions.sendEvents({
  body: {
    profileId: '66a1f0c2a4b9d3e8f1a2b3c4',
    destinations: [{ accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d', destinationId: 'customers/1234567890/conversionActions/987654321' }],
    consent: { adUserData: 'GRANTED', adPersonalization: 'GRANTED' },
    events: [{
      eventName: 'Purchase',
      eventTime: 1798848000,
      eventId: 'order_abc_123',
      value: 129.99,
      currency: 'USD',
      user: {
        email: 'customer@example.com',
        phone: '+14155551234',
        clickIds: { gclid: 'EAIaIQobChMI...' }
      }
    }]
  }
});

console.log(sent.destinations);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
from zernio import Zernio

client = Zernio()

sent = client.conversions.send_events(
    profile_id="66a1f0c2a4b9d3e8f1a2b3c4",
    destinations=[{"accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d", "destinationId": "customers/1234567890/conversionActions/987654321"}],
    consent={"adUserData": "GRANTED", "adPersonalization": "GRANTED"},
    events=[{
        "eventName": "Purchase",
        "eventTime": 1798848000,
        "eventId": "order_abc_123",
        "value": 129.99,
        "currency": "USD",
        "user": {
            "email": "customer@example.com",
            "phone": "+14155551234",
            "clickIds": {"gclid": "EAIaIQobChMI..."},
        },
    }],
)

print(sent["destinations"])
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/events" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "profileId": "66a1f0c2a4b9d3e8f1a2b3c4",
    "destinations": [{ "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d", "destinationId": "customers/1234567890/conversionActions/987654321" }],
    "consent": { "adUserData": "GRANTED", "adPersonalization": "GRANTED" },
    "events": [{
      "eventName": "Purchase",
      "eventTime": 1798848000,
      "eventId": "order_abc_123",
      "value": 129.99,
      "currency": "USD",
      "user": {
        "email": "customer@example.com",
        "phone": "+14155551234",
        "clickIds": { "gclid": "EAIaIQobChMI..." }
      }
    }]
  }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "eventsReceived": 1,
  "stored": true,
  "testCode": null,
  "destinations": [
    { "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d", "destinationId": "customers/1234567890/conversionActions/987654321", "platform": "googleads", "eventsSent": 1, "eventsFailed": 0, "failures": [] }
  ],
  "queuedDestinations": 0
}
```

Conversions take up to 3 hours to appear in Google Ads reports.

Each request takes up to 2,000 events, and Zernio chunks larger batches automatically.

### EEA and UK consent

Google enforces consent signaling for European users under the February 2026 Data Manager restrictions.

Pass `consent` at the request root with `adUserData` and `adPersonalization` set to `GRANTED` or `DENIED`.

Omit the field for non-EEA requests where you have no consent data. Google applies region defaults.

### Deduplication

Pass a stable `eventId` on every event. Zernio maps it to Google's `transactionId`, so repeated uploads of the same conversion are deduped.

## Find a conversion action

Call `GET /v1/ads/conversions/destinations`. It returns every enabled conversion action across the accessible customers.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data: destinations } = await zernio.conversions.listAdConversionDestinations({
  query: { accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d' }
});

console.log(destinations.destinations);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
destinations = client.conversions.list_ad_conversion_destinations(account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d")

print(destinations["destinations"])
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/conversions/destinations?accountId=66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY"
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "platform": "googleads",
  "destinations": [
    { "id": "customers/1234567890/conversionActions/987654321", "name": "Offline purchase", "type": "PURCHASE", "status": "active" }
  ]
}
```

`id` is the conversion action resource name, and `type` its category (`PURCHASE`, `LEAD`, `SIGN_UP`, ...).

Google locks the event type to the conversion action, not to the per-event `eventName`. When no listed action fits, [create one for uploads](#create-a-conversion-action-for-uploads).

## Create a conversion action for uploads

When no existing action fits, call `POST /v1/ads/conversions/destinations` with `accountId`, `adAccountId`, `name` and `type`. `type` takes either form:

- a unified name such as `Purchase`, `Subscribe`, `CompleteRegistration`, `Lead` or `Schedule`
- a Google `ConversionActionCategory` value such as `PURCHASE`, `SUBSCRIBE_PAID`, `SIGNUP`, `IMPORTED_LEAD` or `BOOK_APPOINTMENT`

Google creates it with `type=UPLOAD_CLICKS`, which is immutable after creation.

Calling again with the same name reuses the existing action. The same name with a different category returns `409` with code `idempotency_conflict`.

**Google-only fields:**

- `countingType`: `MANY_PER_CLICK` (the default) or `ONE_PER_CLICK`.
- `primaryForGoal`: default `false`, so the action is record-only until you opt it into Smart Bidding.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/conversions/destinations" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d", "adAccountId": "1234567890", "name": "Offline purchase", "type": "Purchase" }'
```

Response (`201`):

```json
{
  "platform": "googleads",
  "destination": { "id": "customers/1234567890/conversionActions/987654321", "name": "Offline purchase", "type": "PURCHASE", "status": "active" }
}
```

The `id` it returns is the `destinationId` for the upload above.

## Website tag actions

Website conversion actions with their tag snippets (the gtag.js code a customer pastes onto their site) are a separate surface from the upload actions above.

`GET /v1/ads/conversions/actions` lists them, and `POST /v1/ads/conversions/actions` creates a `WEBPAGE` action ([List conversion actions](/conversions/list-conversion-actions)).

The list returns every action type by default (filter with `type`). Each action carries `origin` and `primaryForGoal`, which place it in the [conversion goals](#conversion-goals) below.

The same `WEBPAGE` actions are the events of the account's [Google tag](/platforms/google-ads/tracking-tag), which also installs them on Shopify and WordPress.

## Conversion goals

Google bids on goals, not on individual actions.

A goal is a category and origin pair (for example `PURCHASE` from `WEBSITE`). Every conversion action with that category and origin belongs to it.

Three switches decide what a campaign optimizes for:

| Switch | Where | Endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| `biddable` on an account goal | Account default, followed by every campaign at `goalConfigLevel: CUSTOMER` | [`GET`](/conversions/list-ad-conversion-goals) and [`PATCH /v1/ads/conversions/goals`](/conversions/update-ad-conversion-goals) |
| `primaryForGoal` on an action | Primary actions count toward bidding and the Conversions column; secondary ones are observation-only (All conversions) | [`PATCH /v1/ads/conversions/actions/{actionId}`](/conversions/update-conversion-action) |
| Campaign goals or a custom goal | One campaign, at `goalConfigLevel: CAMPAIGN` | [`GET`](/ad-campaigns/get-campaign-conversion-goals) and [`PATCH /v1/ads/campaigns/{campaignId}/conversion-goals`](/ad-campaigns/update-campaign-conversion-goals) |

All of these take `accountId`. Add `adAccountId` (the customer id) when the connection has several Google customers.

Reads are cached for 10 minutes. They fall back to the last successful copy with `stale: true` when Google's quota runs out.

### Account goals

`GET /v1/ads/conversions/goals` lists the account-default goals, one per category and origin. Each has `biddable` and its conversion actions flagged `primaryForGoal`:

```bash
curl "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/conversions/goals?accountId=66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d&adAccountId=1234567890" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY"
```

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "customerId": "1234567890",
  "goals": [
    {
      "category": "PURCHASE",
      "origin": "WEBSITE",
      "biddable": true,
      "resourceName": "customers/1234567890/customerConversionGoals/PURCHASE~WEBSITE",
      "conversionActions": [
        { "id": "987654321", "name": "Offline purchase", "status": "ENABLED", "primaryForGoal": true }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "cachedAt": "2027-01-31T08:00:00.000Z",
  "stale": false
}
```

`PATCH` on the same path sets `biddable` on up to 100 goals in one mutate, addressed by `category` and `origin`. It returns the re-read list.

Campaigns at `goalConfigLevel: CUSTOMER` follow the change.

```bash
curl -X PATCH "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/conversions/goals" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    "adAccountId": "1234567890",
    "goals": [{ "category": "SIGNUP", "origin": "WEBSITE", "biddable": false }]
  }'
```

### Primary and secondary actions

Flip one action between primary and secondary with `PATCH /v1/ads/conversions/actions/{actionId}`. `actionId` is Google's numeric conversion action id:

```bash
curl -X PATCH "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/conversions/actions/987654321" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d", "primaryForGoal": false }'
```

Response (`200`): `{ "customerId": "1234567890", "action": { "id": "987654321", "primaryForGoal": false } }`.

A primary action only drives bidding when its goal is `biddable`.

Actions you [create for uploads](#create-a-conversion-action-for-uploads) start secondary unless you pass `primaryForGoal: true`.

### Custom goals

A custom goal is a named set of conversion actions a campaign can bid on instead of a category.

- [`POST /v1/ads/conversions/custom-goals`](/conversions/create-custom-conversion-goal) creates one from `name` and `conversionActionIds` (1 to 100 numeric ids), and returns its `id`.
- [`GET`](/conversions/list-custom-conversion-goals) lists them.
- [`PATCH .../custom-goals/{goalId}`](/conversions/update-custom-conversion-goal) renames it or replaces its whole action set.
- [`DELETE`](/conversions/remove-custom-conversion-goal) removes it.

Google refuses the delete (`400`) while any campaign still uses the goal, so switch those campaigns first.

### Campaign goals

`GET /v1/ads/campaigns/{campaignId}/conversion-goals` reads one campaign's goals (`biddable` per category and origin), its `goalConfigLevel` and its `customConversionGoalId`.

- `CUSTOMER` means the campaign follows the account goals.
- `CAMPAIGN` means it uses its own goals or the custom goal.

`PATCH` on the same path changes any of the three in one mutate and returns the re-read state:

```bash
curl -X PATCH "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/campaigns/21874563210/conversion-goals" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "goalConfigLevel": "CAMPAIGN", "customConversionGoalId": "7418529630" }'
```

`customConversionGoalId: null` clears the custom goal.

Google refuses that (`400`) while the campaign stays at `CAMPAIGN` level with no biddable goals. Send `goalConfigLevel: "CUSTOMER"` in the same request to fall back to the account goals.

## Adjust an uploaded conversion

Call `POST /v1/ads/conversions/adjustments` to change a conversion after the fact:

- retract it (refund, chargeback, churn)
- restate its value
- enhance it with first-party identifiers

Identify the original by `orderId` (the `eventId` you sent, required for `ENHANCEMENT`) or by `gclid` plus `conversionTime`.

`RESTATEMENT` takes the corrected total in `restatementValue`, not a delta.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/conversions/adjustments" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    "destinationId": "customers/1234567890/conversionActions/987654321",
    "adjustments": [{ "adjustmentType": "RETRACTION", "adjustmentTime": 1799107200, "orderId": "order_abc_123" }]
  }'
```

Response (`200`):

```json
{ "platform": "googleads", "adjustmentsReceived": 1, "adjustmentsFailed": 0, "failures": [] }
```

Adjustments go through the classic Google Ads API, so this endpoint is Google-only. Meta and LinkedIn return `405`.

## If it fails

| Error | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `200` with `eventsFailed` above 0 | Google rejected some events, such as `CONSENT_REQUIRED` for EEA users | Fix the events `failures[]` names and resend only those |
| `409` `idempotency_conflict` on a conversion action create | The name exists with a different category | Pick another name, or reuse the existing action |
| `405` on adjustments | The account is Meta or LinkedIn, and adjustments are Google-only | Send adjustments for Google accounts only |

`failures[]` names each rejected event by `eventIndex` and `eventId`:

```json
{
  "eventsReceived": 1,
  "stored": true,
  "testCode": null,
  "destinations": [
    { "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d", "destinationId": "customers/1234567890/conversionActions/987654321", "platform": "googleads", "eventsSent": 0, "eventsFailed": 1, "failures": [ { "eventIndex": 0, "eventId": "order_abc_123", "message": "Consent is required for EEA users", "code": "CONSENT_REQUIRED" } ] }
  ],
  "queuedDestinations": 0
}
```

The status is `200` even on partial failure. Branch on each destination's `eventsFailed`, fix the named events and resend only those.
